study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier/name given in the paper text.

subject_id.notes: Individual subject identifiers not provided in main text (may exist in supplemental Table S1).

sample_id.notes: No per-sample identifiers reported in the visible text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within paper text; provided externally as paper_id.

subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Destination groups (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) exist but paper reports aggregate study-level statistics rather than per-subject subcohort assignment in visible text.

target_condition.notes: Study investigates antibiotic resistance gene acquisition and ESBL colonization during international travel, not a specific disease phenotype matching typical target_condition ontology terms.

control.notes: Study is a longitudinal before/after travel design without explicit case/control labeling of samples.

country.evidence_quote: 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden
country.notes: Both before- and after-travel fecal specimens were collected in Sweden (before departure and after return).

body_site.evidence_quote: shotgun metagenomic sequencing to address the abundance of >300 antibiotic resistance genes in fecal specimens

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: The fecal specimens were collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden.
days_from_first_collection.notes: Only aggregate median/range values reported for pre- and post-travel collection timing, not per-sample days from first collection.

location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
location.notes: Recruitment sites in Sweden; travel destinations were Indian peninsula and Central Africa.

westernized.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg
westernized.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
westernized.notes: Inferred from being Swedish university students; not explicitly labeled 'westernized' in text.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction kit not specified in the main text; may be detailed in supplemental methods.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
sequencing_platform.notes: Isolate genomes (ESBL-positive) were separately sequenced using Illumina MiSeq (250-bp paired-end reads).

age.notes: Reported only as a range across all 35 subjects (study-level), not per-subject values; type mismatch with numeric schema field.

age_group.notes: Derived from reported age range (23-34 years), which falls entirely within Adult category (>=18 & <65).

ancestry.notes: Nationality (Swedish) is stated but ancestry is not explicitly reported.

sex.notes: Only aggregate gender distribution reported (74% female, 26/35); no per-subject sex values provided in visible text.

age_min.notes: Reported as a range for the whole cohort (n=35).

age_max.notes: Reported as a range for the whole cohort (n=35).

age_years.notes: Only an age range was reported, not individual or mean ages.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Also stated in abstract: 'the increase observed occurred without any antibiotic intake.'

disease.notes: Participants are described as healthy exchange students but health status is not explicitly labeled 'healthy' in the text.

by_subgroup.Central Africa: All travelers to Central Africa used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis
by_subgroup.Indian peninsula: 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Reported per destination subgroup rather than for the whole cohort; overall granularity classified as study_level but this field varies by subgroup.

biomarker_name.notes: These represent fold-change increases in relative abundance of antibiotic resistance gene categories in fecal metagenomes before vs after travel.

disease_response_os.notes: Not applicable; this is a metagenomic/microbiome study, not a survival study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; healthy student travelers, not oncology/clinical performance study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No explicit 'feces_phenotype' categorical measurements reported; fecal specimens were analyzed for microbiome composition and resistance genes rather than a defined phenotype scale.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

value: 35 Swedish health care students traveled to Central Africa (17) or the Indian peninsula (18)
12/18 (67%) travelers to Indian peninsula acquired ESBL-producing E. coli after return; none from Africa
All E. coli ESBL isolates carried CTX-M-15 gene
69% of subjects had travelers' diarrhea during trip
Study approved by regional ethical review board in Umeå, Sweden (2011-357-32M)
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
uncurated_metadata.notes: Aggregated notable study metadata not captured by other schema fields.

host_species.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs
host_species.notes: Species not explicitly stated as 'Homo sapiens' but clearly human participants (Swedish university students).

This paper is a microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene study, not a clinical oncology or survival study; most schema fields (ECOG, tumor size, OS) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
